rocm.amd_smi: AMDSMI Tool: 26.5.0+03d8462e | AMDSMI Library version: 26.5.0 | ROCm version: 7.15.0 | amdgpu version: 7.1.1.31500000 | ionic version: N/A

question: T_SOL for a compute-bound workload is a cycle count divided by a frequency. Task 01 measured one frequency, 1300 MHz, under a dense bf16 matrix-core load. Is that the frequency the part holds for every kind of arithmetic, or only for that one?
answer: Only for that one, and the exception is large. Every matrix-core path sits at F_LOCK -- bf16 1296, fp16 1299, fp8 1314. The fp32 vector path sustains 1441 MHz, 10.8% above it, because it draws far less power and `--setperfdeterminism 1600` caps the ceiling rather than pinning the clock. Every compute-bound fp32 bound in manifest v1 is therefore 10.8% too large in milliseconds.
method: One saturating 8192-cube GEMM per datapath on an idle GPU 0, amdsmi GFX clock sampled every 2-5 ms for the whole run, on the physical card resolved by PCI bus (scripts/gpu_map.py -- the amdsmi and torch index spaces are scrambled on this node). `clk_steady_last5s_mhz` is the figure to use: the first second is boost, not a frequency any bound may be divided by. Nothing here changed a determinism setting or a power cap.
use: Divide t_sol_cycles by the clock of the datapath SOLAR priced the workload at. The datapath is recoverable without a new field: macs / t_sol_cycles_exact lands exactly on one of the MAC_per_cycle entries in src/solexbench_rocm/parts.py -- 836 fp32_sm, 953 bf16/fp16_tc and 46 fp8/int8_tc across the manifest, with nothing unmatched.
not_affected: Memory-bound bounds. The traffic tier computes cycles = bytes / DRAM_byte_per_cycle and then ms = cycles / freq, and DRAM_byte_per_cycle is itself bytes-per-second / freq -- so ms = bytes / bytes-per-second and the frequency cancels exactly. This is algebra, not an observation, and it is why only the compute tier moves.
caveats: fp64 was not measured: no problem in the dataset declares float64, and the 8192-cube fp64 GEMM flooded the submission queue faster than it drained.

Idle node, one card. Under a loaded node the power budget is shared and these clocks would be lower. Scoring runs on an idle node by design, so the idle-node clock is the one a scored measurement is compared against.

One shape per datapath. A workload that saturates a datapath differently -- a small GEMM, a memory-bound kernel with an arithmetic tail -- may sit elsewhere between 1296 and 1586 MHz; 1586 was observed on a real agent kernel (artifacts/11/bound-violations-diagnosis.json). Using the saturating-GEMM clock is the conservative choice for a lower bound: it is the lowest clock at which that datapath runs flat out, so the bound it produces is the largest defensible one.
